A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. Appendices A–D are retained; v2 adds experimental Appendix E.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical results and proofs, including an analytical two-point construction. Figure 1 is schematic and Table 1 summarizes theoretical bounds; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: V2 reports original gradient-descent simulations on a two-point separable dataset in Figure 2 and Appendix E, including Figure 3.

M1.justification: The regularized logistic objective and constant-stepsize gradient-descent update are unchanged. The new simulations implement the existing procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds one synthetic evaluation dataset: x1=(0.2,1), x2=(0.2,-2), with both labels +1. V1 contains no numerical evaluation. Its different two-point theoretical lower-bound construction remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The new plots compare stepsize configurations of the same GD algorithm, without introducing another comparison method. Table 1 retains its theoretical comparisons with Nesterov’s momentum and adaptive GD; neither receives a new experimental evaluation.

E3.justification: The new simulation uses regularization 2^-12, zero initialization, 2^13 iterations and a logarithmic stepsize sweep from 2^1 to 2^13. It tracks objective values, Hessian sharpness, parameter trajectories and loss components. These are newly introduced settings, not revisions to an earlier experiment.

E4.justification: Figures 2–3 add a limited stepsize-sensitivity case study examining acceleration, nonconvergence at excessive stepsizes, and the separate evolution of logistic and regularization terms. V1 provides theoretical discussion but no corresponding numerical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2’s deterministic toy simulations introduce no uncertainty-estimation procedure. The theoretical high-probability population-risk bounds are retained.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports faster convergence with larger convergent stepsizes, convergence through eta=32, and nonconvergence at larger tested stepsizes. At eta=32, the loss components remain nonmonotone after the total objective stops oscillating around step 16. These are new illustrative findings; Table 1’s theoretical rates remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The numbered assumptions, results and proofs in Appendices A–D are unchanged. Section 1 qualifies the mathematical assertion of eventual monotonicity to generic initializations. Appendix E also introduces a local-stability expression, incorrectly printed using the gradient at the minimizer rather than the Hessian.

C1.justification: The abstract and three central contributions retain their meaning: acceleration under small and general regularization, population-risk acceleration, and a critical stepsize threshold. V2 makes existing regularization conditions more explicit without changing these core results.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 newly explains that Corollaries 2 and 5 give incomparable bounds, with their relative advantage switching around lambda=n^-3/2, and identifies room to improve the analysis. V2 adds open questions about larger regularization and nonseparable data, narrows the suggested neural-network extension to two-layer networks with bi-Lipschitz activations, and connects the simulations to the existing mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds a code-repository link, identifies JAX, supplies the exact synthetic data and simulation settings, and reports execution in a few seconds on a consumer laptop. V1 contains no corresponding implementation or code-access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds Cohen et al. (2025) on central flows, Meng et al. (2025) on logistic-regression dynamics, and Bradbury et al. (2018) for JAX. These are limited additions to the retained positioning. The changed year of the earlier Cohen citation refers to the same work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the ordering of Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–D are retained. V2 adds a simulations paragraph and Appendix E, expands selected explanations and limitations, and updates author affiliations and publication information.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a conference template that changes the title and author block, typography, spacing and text area throughout. It adds a three-panel Figure 2 and four-panel Figure 3; Figure 3 repeats one objective plot while adding other views. Figure 1 is retained, and the unchanged Table 1 is relocated.

improvement.justification: The numerical illustrations, reproducibility details and more precise discussion of limitations make the retained theory easier to understand and assess. The gain is limited because empirical support remains one toy example and the main proofs are unchanged. These benefits outweigh a localized defect in Appendix E, whose stability-threshold formula incorrectly uses the gradient at the minimizer instead of the Hessian.
